concepts.name: Online marketing channels
concepts.summary: Name and distinguish the main channels such as paid search, social media, email, display and organic search, and what each is used for.

concepts.name: Campaign goals
concepts.summary: Explain why every campaign starts with a specific goal such as awareness, traffic, leads or sales and how the goal shapes later choices.

concepts.name: Target audience
concepts.summary: Describe who a campaign is meant to reach, using basic demographics and interests, and why message and channel must fit that audience.

concepts.name: Marketing funnel stages
concepts.summary: Explain how people move from awareness through consideration to purchase and why different content suits each stage.

concepts.name: Pay-per-click model
concepts.summary: Explain that advertisers pay when users click (or see) an ad, and how this differs from organic reach.

concepts.name: Core ad metrics
concepts.summary: Define impressions, clicks, click-through rate and conversions and state what each one counts.

concepts.name: Call to action
concepts.summary: Explain why a clear, single next step in an ad or email drives action and recognise strong versus vague examples.

misconceptions.text: More impressions always mean a campaign is succeeding.
Social media posting alone is a complete marketing strategy.
A campaign can target everyone and still work well.

concepts.name: Conversion rate calculation
concepts.summary: Calculate conversion rate from clicks and conversions and interpret it for a simple campaign.

concepts.name: Cost per click and CPA
concepts.summary: Compute CPC and cost per acquisition from spend and results and compare campaigns with them.

concepts.name: Keyword and search ad setup
concepts.summary: Build a basic search campaign with ad groups, keywords, match types and ad copy tied to search intent.

concepts.name: Social ad targeting options
concepts.summary: Configure audiences on a social ad platform using location, demographics, interests and custom lists.

concepts.name: Email list and newsletter basics
concepts.summary: Build a permission-based list, write a subject line and send a newsletter, tracking open and click rates.

concepts.name: Landing page alignment
concepts.summary: Match a landing page's message and call to action to the ad that leads to it.

concepts.name: Simple A/B test
concepts.summary: Run a test that changes one element, such as a subject line, between two versions and read the result.

concepts.name: Reading analytics reports
concepts.summary: Read sessions, traffic sources and conversion data in an analytics report to see what each channel delivers.

misconceptions.text: A high click-through rate means the ad is profitable.
Broad match keywords are always the best way to get more customers.
Testing several changes at once in an A/B test shows which change worked.

concepts.name: ROAS and profitability
concepts.summary: Calculate ROAS and compare it with break-even ROAS based on margin to judge whether a campaign is profitable.

concepts.name: Funnel-based KPI selection
concepts.summary: Choose KPIs for each funnel stage and campaign goal and separate meaningful metrics from vanity metrics.

concepts.name: Conversion tracking setup
concepts.summary: Set up tracking of conversion events with tags, pixels and UTM parameters so results can be tied to campaigns.

concepts.name: Audience segmentation and retargeting
concepts.summary: Segment audiences by behaviour and funnel position and design retargeting and lookalike audiences with suitable messages.

concepts.name: Statistical validity of tests
concepts.summary: Judge whether an A/B test has enough sample and duration to support a decision, accounting for significance and random variation.

concepts.name: Email automation flows
concepts.summary: Design triggered sequences such as welcome and abandoned-cart flows based on behaviour and segmentation.

concepts.name: Budget allocation across channels
concepts.summary: Divide a budget across channels by comparing CPA and ROAS and by funnel role, not on last-click results alone.

concepts.name: Dashboard building
concepts.summary: Build a dashboard that presents the KPIs stakeholders need and enables comparison over time and by channel.

misconceptions.text: A ROAS above 1 means a campaign is profitable.
An A/B test can be stopped as soon as one variant pulls ahead.
The channel that gets the last click deserves the credit for the sale.

concepts.name: Attribution model evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate last-click, first-click, linear and data-driven attribution and judge how each shifts credit and budget decisions.

concepts.name: Customer lifetime value economics
concepts.summary: Judge acquisition spend against customer lifetime value and payback period, not only first-purchase CPA.

concepts.name: Bid strategy and auction dynamics
concepts.summary: Analyse how ad auctions, quality, bids and automated bidding strategies influence cost and reach, and choose among strategies.

concepts.name: Creative testing framework
concepts.summary: Plan a systematic programme of creative and offer tests, prioritise hypotheses and judge results.

concepts.name: Cross-channel journey analysis
concepts.summary: Analyse how channels work together along multi-touch journeys to find gaps, overlap and assisted conversions.

concepts.name: Privacy and data constraints
concepts.summary: Analyse how consent rules and platform tracking limits reduce measurement accuracy and adjust tactics, such as first-party data use.

concepts.name: Incrementality measurement
concepts.summary: Design holdout or geo experiments to estimate the sales a campaign truly caused rather than only those it was credited with.

misconceptions.text: Platform-reported conversions equal the sales the ads caused.
The lowest CPA channel should always receive the most budget.
Automated smart bidding removes the need for human strategy and good conversion data.

concepts.name: Marketing mix modelling
concepts.summary: Evaluate when and how statistical models of aggregate spend and sales support budget decisions, and their limits.

concepts.name: Triangulated measurement design
concepts.summary: Create a measurement framework that combines attribution, experiments and modelling and reconciles their conflicting answers.

concepts.name: Marginal return budget optimisation
concepts.summary: Build budget plans using response curves and marginal ROAS or CPA, reallocating spend until marginal returns equalise.

concepts.name: Integrated growth strategy
concepts.summary: Design a strategy balancing brand-building and performance activity, linked to business goals, margins and lifetime value.

concepts.name: Experimentation programme governance
concepts.summary: Evaluate and set up processes for prioritising, running and learning from experiments across teams, including multiple-testing risks.

concepts.name: Marketing automation architecture
concepts.summary: Design lifecycle automation across email, ads and CRM using first-party data, with suppression, personalisation and frequency rules.

concepts.name: Forecasting and scenario planning
concepts.summary: Judge forecasts of cost, revenue and risk under different budgets and market conditions and communicate the uncertainty to leaders.

misconceptions.text: One measurement method, such as attribution or a mix model, can be trusted as the single source of truth.
If average ROAS is strong, spending more will keep returns at the same level.
Brand advertising cannot be measured, so it should be cut in favour of performance channels.
